request.system:
You check job postings for one job seeker, Cole. You write short, checkable claims about whether one posting fits Cole, and you tie each claim to the exact words of the posting.

INPUT
The user message is a JSON object with:
- "posting_id": the posting's id (a string).
- "title" and "locations": the posting's title and listed locations, for context only.
- "posting_text": the posting text. This is the ONLY text you may quote.
- "cole": what Cole is looking for: target_titles, years_experience, needs_sponsorship, work_country, skills.

TASK
Write 3 to 6 claims. Each claim is one checkable statement that, if the posting supports it, means the posting fits Cole on that point. Examples of the shape: "The role is a software engineering role." "The job can be done in the US." "The role requires at most 2 years of experience." "The employer will sponsor a work visa." "The work uses Python."
Write at least one claim of each of these kinds: role, location, experience, sponsorship. You may add claims of kind seniority or skill, up to 6 claims in total.

For each claim give:
- "kind": one of role, seniority, location, experience, sponsorship, skill.
- "claim": the statement.
- "quote": one contiguous span copied character for character from posting_text, the span that best decides the claim. Copy it exactly: no ellipses, no paraphrase, no corrected spelling or punctuation, no added quotation marks, nothing from title or locations. Keep it to the sentence or list item that decides the claim. If nothing in posting_text speaks to the claim, use "" (empty string).
- "proposed_label": supported, contradicted or insufficient, using the definitions below. If "quote" is "", the label must be insufficient.

LABEL DEFINITIONS (from FILTER.md, word for word)
The shortlist explains each keep with **claims**. A claim is one checkable statement about the posting, for example "requires at most 2 years", "US-based", or "the work uses Python".
- supported: A span quoted verbatim from the posting text asserts the claim. The quote must exist in the text. Its meaning must assert the claim, not just mention the word.
- contradicted: A quoted span asserts the opposite of the claim.
- insufficient: No span asserts the claim either way, or the only span mentions the word without asserting it (a "nice to have", a team description, boilerplate).
**Relevance is not entailment.** A posting that contains "Python" in a "nice to have" list is relevant to a Python claim, but does not support "the role requires Python." That claim is insufficient.

Do not guess. A claim the posting does not settle is insufficient, not supported. Company boilerplate and benefits text do not support a claim about the role.

OUTPUT
Return ONLY one JSON object, with no other text before or after it:
{"posting_id": "<the posting_id from the input>", "claims": [{"kind": "role|seniority|location|experience|sponsorship|skill", "claim": "...", "quote": "...", "proposed_label": "supported|contradicted|insufficient"}]}

{
  "posting_id": "8131144",
  "title": "Backend Engineer, Link",
  "locations": [
    "NYC, Sea, SF, Tor"
  ],
  "posting_text": "Who we are About the team Link is a digital wallet designed for effortless and secure online payments and digital transactions. With Link, consumers enjoy convenience and peace of mind—it works on any device or browser, is backed by the highest security mechanisms, offers purchase protections on eligible items, and ensures seamless and quick payments. Across the Link Engineering org, we focus on building delightful payment experiences and allowing our global consumer base to pay with their preferred payment methods. Our team's work spans the entire stack from front-end experiences, to infrastructure that supports low-latency transactions, to intelligent systems that help protect consumers and merchants from bad actors. Team matching for one of the subteams will begin during final stages. Please note we may also consider you for different orgs based on your experience, location, etc. More information on our team matching process can be found here . What you'll do We're looking for engineers who want to make an impact on payments at a global scale. You'll play a key role in expanding our product suite and the infrastructure that supports it. Our team collaborates with many cross-functional teams and many other teams across Stripe to deliver innovative solutions that address evolving user needs. Responsibilities Build and design the next generation of Stripe products to meet the high-growth needs of our company and customers for years to come Debug and solve critical production issues across services and multiple levels of the stack Mentor engineers to help them grow Collaborate with stakeholders across the company to build new features at large-scale, while improving internal engineering standards, tooling, and processes Collaborate effectively in a distributed and hybrid team, maintaining open communication and strong connections with colleagues Who you are We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement. Minimum requirements 2–10+ years of industry software engineering experience (does not include internships or co-ops) Strong coding skills in any programming language Strong collaboration skills and the ability to work across workstreams within your team and contribute to your peers' success Ability to thrive with a high level of autonomy and responsibility and an entrepreneurial mindset Interest in working as a backend specialist across varying technologies and stacks to solve problems and delight both internal and external users Preferred qualifications Experience with large-scale financial tracking systems Good understanding and practical knowledge in cloud-based services Experience with, or enthusiasm for, building with AI and agentic workflows",
  "cole": {
    "target_titles": [
      "Software Engineer",
      "AI Engineer",
      "Backend Engineer"
    ],
    "years_experience": 0,
    "needs_sponsorship": true,
    "work_country": "US",
    "skills": [
      "Python",
      "Java",
      "TypeScript",
      "SQL",
      "PostgreSQL",
      "Spring Boot",
      "React",
      "Docker",
      "AWS"
    ]
  }
}
